newsitem.title: FRANCE: France has record trade surplus, outlook improving.
newsitem.headline: France has record trade surplus, outlook improving.

text.p: The French government, fighting deep unpopularity, received welcome news Tuesday as the October trade surplus posted a record high and a December industry survey showed the outlook continues to improve.

But the positive data, combined with a 25 percent gain on the Paris Bourse for the 1996 trading year and anecdotal evidence of a rush to the shops before Christmas, came against a background of a record 12.6 percent unemployment rate.

The customs office said the seasonally adjusted trade surplus in October widened to 16.94 billion French franc ($3.23 billion) from a revised surplus in September of 9.70 billion francs ($1.85 billion).

More significantly, the surplus was not due to one-time factors such as exceptional sales of Airbus planes or defence exports. The October figure included 3.64 billion francs ($695 million), or eight aircraft sales, against 2.33 billion frances ($445 million) for six planes in September.
Defence exports were down 770 million francs ($147 million) from 1.10 billion ($210 million).
The higher surplus was the result of slowing imports and rising exports in industrial and agricultural products, while the franc's exchange rate remained stable.

Net exports to the rest of the European Union rose to 6.18 billion francs ($1.18 billion) from 4.44 billion ($847 million) while the trade deficit with the United States was slashed to 1.11 billion francs ($212 million) from 2.57 billion ($490 million).

"These results confirm the dynamic exports of French technology and the competitiveness of companies," Trade Minister Yves Galland said in a statement. Resumed grain sales boosted agricultural exports, he added.
The rising surplus was attained despite rising prices for oil, which boosted France's energy deficit to 7.7 billion francs ($1.47 billion) from 6.2 billion ($1.18 billion), Galland said.
The Finance Ministry said the running total for the year was for a surplus of 121.9 billion francs ($23.3 billion).

The INSEE national statistics office said its industrial survey showed business leaders had become more optimistic. "The general outlook for production is continuing to improve, even though the personal outlook is hardly changing and indicates moderate growth in the next three months," INSEE said in a statement.
